abstract: Measures AI's macroeconomic effect through software-engineering productivity using financial markets: estimates each firm's stock-return sensitivity to an AI stock index and how it depends on the firm's payroll share in software engineering, then maps this into productivity and GDP with a model.
keyFindings: From November 2022 to December 2025, AI raised the market's expected present value of software-engineering productivity by the equivalent of a permanent 32.6% productivity increase.
Implied effect on the level of GDP: 3.6% in the baseline, 6.5% when higher software-engineering productivity also raises R&D productivity.
By mid-2026, amid rapid progress in coding agents, the effect on productivity and GDP had more than doubled relative to end-2025.
methodology: Cross-sectional asset-pricing estimates mapped through a structural model; forward-looking, real-time measure.
qualifiers: Market-expectation measure of present value, not realized productivity or output.
Abstract-level extraction; NBER full text was not accessible to scripts.
